bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to environment; requiring public water supplies and publicly owned treatment works to annually report on water access policies; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 115.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[115.85] WATER ACCESS REPORT REQUIRED.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Appropriate agency" means:

(1) the commissioner of health for a public water supply; and

(2) the commissioner of the Pollution Control Agency for a publicly owned treatment works.

(c) "Public water supply" has the meaning given to public water system in the federal Safe Drinking Water Act, United States Code, title 42, section 300f, clause (4).

(d) "Water access report" means a report containing the information described in subdivision 2.

(e) "Water utility" means any of the following operating in this state:

(1) a public water supply; or

(2) a publicly owned treatment works.

Subd. 2.

Report required.

Each year by March 1, a water utility must submit to the appropriate agency a water access report that:

(1) explains the policies the water utility had in place during the previous calendar year with respect to each of the following, including information about the method, content, and frequency with which information about each was communicated to customers:

(i) late payments and termination of service and related fees and charges;

(ii) payment plan options;

(iii) any alternative rate structures or available financial assistance; and

(iv) local ordinances that control any of the policies described in items (i) to (iii);

(2) includes the following information for the previous calendar year, stated separately for residential, commercial, and industrial accounts:

(i) total number of accounts;

(ii) total number of accounts terminated or suspended for nonpayment; and

(iii) number of accounts terminated or suspended for nonpayment, stated separately for nonpayment of water bill, nonpayment of wastewater bill, and nonpayment of both and broken out by month of termination or suspension; and

(3) includes the following additional information:

(i) contact information for the water utility that customers can use to discuss bills, seek assistance, or address termination of service;

(ii) a balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement for the most recently concluded fiscal year; and

(iii) when applicable, an explanation of the reason that the water utility is unable to supply any of the information required by this subdivision.

Subd. 3.

Posting required.

The appropriate agency must post a water access report received from a water utility on the agency's website.

Subd. 4.

Providing information.

Any person that possesses information that must be included in a report required under subdivision 2 must provide that information to the reporting water utility upon request.
